tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
The guardrails are in [PR #223](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/223): comments are banned by lint and removed, imports now flow one way, and AGENTS.md covers the desktop app. Lint, typecheck, build and the bundle budget pass. Unit tests pass (1,701) only with a longer timeout on this machine; at the default 5 seconds a few time out, and the subagent found the same failures on a copy without these changes. Playwright and the desktop build were not run.

## What changed

- **Comment ban:** a lint rule, `moneo/no-comments`, rejects every comment except tool directives such as `eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- reason` and `@ts-expect-error`. Its error tells the agent to put the meaning in a name, type, test or lint rule, and `eslint --fix` deletes the comment.
- **Comments removed:** the subagent stripped 3,133 comments from 588 files with that autofix, with no code changes. I read "high-Q" as Haiku, so that is the model it ran on.
- **One-way imports:** `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`, enforced by lint. Lint also stops `lib/finance` importing `lib/ai`, Electron imports outside `desktop/src`, and app code inside `desktop/src`.
- **Modules moved to make that true:** net-worth logic, the transaction amount parser, recurring schedules/suggestions/series, two server-action files, the chat form and the net-worth chart all left `app/` for `lib/` or `components/`.
- **AGENTS.md:** adds "never write a comment", "corrections become checks", the import layering, and a Desktop app section covering what the Electron build changes for anyone editing the code.

Not touched: comments in SQL migrations (applied migrations must not be rewritten), CSS, YAML and `.env.example`. Say if you want the non-migration ones gone too.

## What else from the talk fits Moneo

In rough order of value:

1. **Restrict `useEffect` and timers in product code.** There are 75 `useEffect` calls in 42 files and 25 timers in 19, mostly polling and auto-dismiss. 3. **Screenshots and videos on the PR, not diffs.** Have Playwright attach before/after screenshots or a short recording for any changed flow, so you review what the app does.
4. **Property-based tests for money math.** `fast-check` on the `lib/finance` invariants (splits sum to the total, undo restores the exact state, currency conversion round-trips within tolerance). This is the cheap version of her Lean and TLA+ work, and it fits "financial truth comes from code".
5. **Feature map.** One generated file listing every page, widget, chat tool and command-palette entry. It would replace most of the "Hit every surface" prose with something a test can check.
6. **Outer loop, last.** The nightly browser run already exists; letting it open fix PRs on its own is the final step, once the items above are in.

Skills I would add:

- **`verify-ui`:** drives the QA server on port 3100, captures before/after screenshots in light, dark and mobile, and attaches them to the PR.
- **`review-to-rule`:** takes a review correction and turns it into a lint rule or test with a descriptive error.
- **`state-chart`:** draws the state machine for a flow (import, bank reconnect, voice call) as a diagram to review beside the screenshots.

I'd skip TLA+ and Lean for now; nothing in Moneo is concurrent enough to earn them except possibly the reservation race, which already has a live test.

# Browser tests

Playwright tests run against the separate test backend (Docker project `moneo-qa`, `.env.qa`) and this checkout's app on http://localhost:3100. The config starts the app with `npm run qa:server` (or a production build with `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`) unless it is already running.

## Setup

1. Create the test backend once (and after pulling new migrations): `npm run setup -- --qa`.
2. Create the QA user and save its session: `npm run qa:auth`. Its login is stored in `.env.qa` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, and its session in `e2e/.auth.json` (or set `E2E_STORAGE_STATE`).
3. Before a full run, empty its workspace: `npm run qa:reset`.

The whole test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` and step 1 start it fresh. The owner's `moneo` project is never touched.

Tests never use the owner's workspace. Every spec runs with the saved QA session and an `x-moneo-test` header; with that header the app refuses a request that has no valid session instead of signing the owner in (`proxy.ts`). Before any spec runs, `e2e/global-setup.ts` checks that the server under test does this, so an older or foreign server on the port stops the run.

## Running

```sh
npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1
```

Use one worker: several specs change the same QA workspace and its preferences. The QA server builds into `.next-qa`, so it can run beside `npm run dev`.

## Kinds of specs

- `*.smoke.spec.ts` and `*.mocked.spec.ts` stub or skip the backend. Against a configured backend they still need the QA session, like every spec.
- `*.gated.spec.ts` need the backend. Most use the QA session; others create disposable users with the service key, sign them in by session cookie, and remove them in `finally`. If interrupted, their IDs are left in ignored `.qa/` files for cleanup.
- `*.provider.spec.ts` call the real AI model, so they cost money. They run only with `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; `npm run test:e2e` leaves them out.
- `review-runtime.config.ts` and `review-investigation.config.ts` run the real Workflow engine against local synthetic database and model servers (ports 3040/3041), including a server restart mid-review: `npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts`.

## Nightly

`npm run qa:nightly -- --install` schedules the whole suite for 03:00 every day (a Windows scheduled task that starts as soon as possible if the PC was off). It runs every spec twice on a production build of `origin/main`, in its own worktree in `~/.moneo/nightly`, and keeps one GitHub issue, "Nightly browser suite is failing", up to date. A night with Docker off or port 3100 busy is skipped quietly; the log is `~/.moneo/nightly.log`.

A skipped spec is not a pass: it means a prerequisite (backend, QA session, service key) is missing.

## Scalable

`scalable-trading.provider.spec.ts` drives chat against a local stand-in for Scalable's MCP server (`e2e/mocks/scalable-mcp.mjs`, made-up data) with the real AI model. Start `npm run qa:server` with `SCALABLE_MCP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3043` (and the AI key in `.env.qa`) and run the spec with the same variable and `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; the spec starts the stand-in, adds a Scalable connection to the QA workspace and removes it afterwards. It checks that an order is previewed on a card and sent only when the card is tapped, once, and that read-only access is told it can't trade.

input.prompt:
Read-only audit. Work in the git worktree C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-020838e5-de7d748e8ea1f495 (Windows, Git Bash available). Do not edit, create, commit, stash or push anything, do not start subagents, and do not run anything against Docker, port 3000 or the network. Reading files, `git` read commands, grep, and `npx eslint` / `npx tsc --noEmit` are fine. Do not run the test suite (it is slow and already known to pass).

## Context
Moneo is a local-first personal-finance app: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript, Postgres + Supabase services, an Electron desktop build in `desktop/`. Read `AGENTS.md` first; it holds the project's rules.

The owner wants to stop reviewing AI-written code. The approach, from a talk by Lauren Tan: make the codebase itself the guardrail. In priority order: (1) clean architecture and APIs, (2) lint rules, types and tests that reject bad patterns with error messages that tell the agent what to do instead, (3) runtime verification, (4) as little prose as possible. Weeds (workarounds, anti-patterns, inconsistent patterns) matter because agents copy whatever is already in the code.

The branch `t3/agent-codebase-guardrails` (3 commits ahead of `main`; see `git log main..HEAD` and `git diff main..HEAD --stat`) already did this:
- `moneo/no-comments` lint rule in `eslint.config.mjs`, and all flagged comments removed.
- Import boundaries by lint: `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`; `lib/finance` may not import `lib/ai`; Electron only in `desktop/src`; no app code in `desktop/src`.
- AGENTS.md: comment ban, "corrections become checks", a Desktop app section.

Already known and already proposed to the owner, so do not report these again: 75 raw `useEffect` and 25 raw timers in `app/` and `components/`; 27 `as unknown as` casts of Supabase rows; adding property-based tests for money math; a generated feature map; PR screenshots.

## What I want
Find what we missed. Two parts.

**A. Check the work on this branch.**
- Is the `moneo/no-comments` rule correct? Look for comments it should allow but rejects, or ways to slip prose past it. Check the autofix for cases that could change behaviour.
- Are the boundary rules complete? Look for ways around them (relative paths, dynamic `import()`, `require`, `vi.mock` in non-test files, re-exports) and for file globs they do not cover (`scripts/`, `e2e/`, `supabase/tests/`, root files, `.mts`).
- Did the comment removal delete anything that carried a rule nobody else enforces? Sample `git show 2656bc41` (the removal commit) for comments that stated an invariant, a security reason or a "must not" and check whether a test or lint rule covers that invariant. Report only the ones that are not covered and where breaking it would be a real bug.
- Is the new AGENTS.md text accurate against the code (ports, file names, commands, the desktop section)?

**B. Find weeds and missing guardrails in the rest of the codebase.** Look for patterns an agent would copy and get wrong, where a deterministic check could replace review. Starting points, not a checklist:
- AGENTS.md "Non-negotiables" and "Safety" that are still only prose. For each, could a lint rule, type or test enforce it? Examples: money as `bigint` minor units with explicit currency (look for `number` money, float maths, `Number(` on amounts outside display code); everything listening on `127.0.0.1`; the browser never calling the Supabase URL; AI writes only as cards; no hard-coded ports.
- Two or more ways of doing the same thing (data loading, error handling, form actions, Supabase client creation, env access, date handling, money formatting). Name the variants with file paths and say which should win.
- TypeScript strictness left on the table (`tsconfig.json`), lint rules in `eslint-config-next` / typescript-eslint that are off but would catch real bugs here (floating promises, exhaustive switches, unsafe `any`).
- Server/client leaks: server-only modules importable from `"use client"` files, secrets or `process.env` read in client code.
- Dead code, unused exports and unused dependencies, if you can show them cheaply.
- Very large files or functions that agents will struggle to edit safely.
- CI gaps: checks AGENTS.md says to run that `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not.

## Output
Plain text, most valuable first, at most 15 findings. For each: what it is, evidence (file paths with line numbers, counts), the deterministic check that would enforce it, and rough effort (small / medium / large). Mark each finding as "verified" (you read the code and are sure) or "likely" (inferred). Put anything wrong with the branch's own work (part A) at the top. If a starting point turned up nothing, say so in one line rather than padding. Do not include findings from the "already known" list.

## Context
Moneo is a local-first personal-finance app: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript, Postgres + Supabase services, an Electron desktop build in `desktop/`. Read `AGENTS.md` first; it holds the project's rules.

The owner wants to stop reviewing AI-written code. The approach, from a talk by Lauren Tan: make the codebase itself the guardrail. In priority order: (1) clean architecture and APIs, (2) lint rules, types and tests that reject bad patterns with error messages that tell the agent what to do instead, (3) runtime verification, (4) as little prose as possible. Weeds (workarounds, anti-patterns, inconsistent patterns) matter because agents copy whatever is already in the code.

The branch `t3/agent-codebase-guardrails` (3 commits ahead of `main`; see `git log main..HEAD` and `git diff main..HEAD --stat`) already did this:
- `moneo/no-comments` lint rule in `eslint.config.mjs`, and all flagged comments removed.
- Import boundaries by lint: `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`; `lib/finance` may not import `lib/ai`; Electron only in `desktop/src`; no app code in `desktop/src`.
- AGENTS.md: comment ban, "corrections become checks", a Desktop app section.

Already known and already proposed to the owner, so do not report these again: 75 raw `useEffect` and 25 raw timers in `app/` and `components/`; 27 `as unknown as` casts of Supabase rows; adding property-based tests for money math; a generated feature map; PR screenshots.

Find what we missed. Two parts.

**A. Check the work on this branch.**
- Is the `moneo/no-comments` rule correct? Look for comments it should allow but rejects, or ways to slip prose past it. Check the autofix for cases that could change behaviour.
- Are the boundary rules complete? Look for ways around them (relative paths, dynamic `import()`, `require`, `vi.mock` in non-test files, re-exports) and for file globs they do not cover (`scripts/`, `e2e/`, `supabase/tests/`, root files, `.mts`).
- Did the comment removal delete anything that carried a rule nobody else enforces? Sample `git show 2656bc41` (the removal commit) for comments that stated an invariant, a security reason or a "must not" and check whether a test or lint rule covers that invariant. Report only the ones that are not covered and where breaking it would be a real bug.
- Is the new AGENTS.md text accurate against the code (ports, file names, commands, the desktop section)?

**B. Find weeds and missing guardrails in the rest of the codebase.** Look for patterns an agent would copy and get wrong, where a deterministic check could replace review. Starting points, not a checklist:
- AGENTS.md "Non-negotiables" and "Safety" that are still only prose. For each, could a lint rule, type or test enforce it? Examples: money as `bigint` minor units with explicit currency (look for `number` money, float maths, `Number(` on amounts outside display code); everything listening on `127.0.0.1`; the browser never calling the Supabase URL; AI writes only as cards; no hard-coded ports.
- Two or more ways of doing the same thing (data loading, error handling, form actions, Supabase client creation, env access, date handling, money formatting). Name the variants with file paths and say which should win.
- TypeScript strictness left on the table (`tsconfig.json`), lint rules in `eslint-config-next` / typescript-eslint that are off but would catch real bugs here (floating promises, exhaustive switches, unsafe `any`).
- Server/client leaks: server-only modules importable from `"use client"` files, secrets or `process.env` read in client code.
- Dead code, unused exports and unused dependencies, if you can show them cheaply.
- Very large files or functions that agents will struggle to edit safely.
- CI gaps: checks AGENTS.md says to run that `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not.

# Browser tests

Playwright tests run against the separate test backend (Docker project `moneo-qa`, `.env.qa`) and this checkout's app on http://localhost:3100. The config starts the app with `npm run qa:server` (or a production build with `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`) unless it is already running.

## Setup

1. Create the test backend once (and after pulling new migrations): `npm run setup -- --qa`.
2. Create the QA user and save its session: `npm run qa:auth`. Its login is stored in `.env.qa` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, and its session in `e2e/.auth.json` (or set `E2E_STORAGE_STATE`).
3. Before a full run, empty its workspace: `npm run qa:reset`.

The whole test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` and step 1 start it fresh. The owner's `moneo` project is never touched.

Tests never use the owner's workspace. Every spec runs with the saved QA session and an `x-moneo-test` header; with that header the app refuses a request that has no valid session instead of signing the owner in (`proxy.ts`). Before any spec runs, `e2e/global-setup.ts` checks that the server under test does this, so an older or foreign server on the port stops the run.

## Running

```sh
npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1
```

Use one worker: several specs change the same QA workspace and its preferences. The QA server builds into `.next-qa`, so it can run beside `npm run dev`.

## Kinds of specs

- `*.smoke.spec.ts` and `*.mocked.spec.ts` stub or skip the backend. Against a configured backend they still need the QA session, like every spec.
- `*.gated.spec.ts` need the backend. Most use the QA session; others create disposable users with the service key, sign them in by session cookie, and remove them in `finally`. If interrupted, their IDs are left in ignored `.qa/` files for cleanup.
- `*.provider.spec.ts` call the real AI model, so they cost money. They run only with `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; `npm run test:e2e` leaves them out.
- `review-runtime.config.ts` and `review-investigation.config.ts` run the real Workflow engine against local synthetic database and model servers (ports 3040/3041), including a server restart mid-review: `npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts`.

## Nightly

`npm run qa:nightly -- --install` schedules the whole suite for 03:00 every day (a Windows scheduled task that starts as soon as possible if the PC was off). It runs every spec twice on a production build of `origin/main`, in its own worktree in `~/.moneo/nightly`, and keeps one GitHub issue, "Nightly browser suite is failing", up to date. A night with Docker off or port 3100 busy is skipped quietly; the log is `~/.moneo/nightly.log`.

A skipped spec is not a pass: it means a prerequisite (backend, QA session, service key) is missing.

## Scalable

`scalable-trading.provider.spec.ts` drives chat against a local stand-in for Scalable's MCP server (`e2e/mocks/scalable-mcp.mjs`, made-up data) with the real AI model. Start `npm run qa:server` with `SCALABLE_MCP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3043` (and the AI key in `.env.qa`) and run the spec with the same variable and `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; the spec starts the stand-in, adds a Scalable connection to the QA workspace and removes it afterwards. It checks that an order is previewed on a card and sent only when the card is tapped, once, and that read-only access is told it can't trade.

name: verify-ui

Use after any change to a page, component or style, when asked to "verify the UI", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
---

# Verify a UI change

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. Give them pictures of every page the change touches.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## Steps

1. **List the pages.** Work out every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names (home widgets, the chat panel, mobile layout).
2. **Get the QA app running** if it is not: `npm run setup -- --qa`, `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base), run:
   `npm run qa:shots -- before /path /other/path`
4. **After.** On the changed code, run the same command with `after`.
   Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`. It prints the HTTP status and any browser console errors per page and exits 1 if there were any.
5. **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark, and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
6. **Show the owner.** Put before and after side by side in the PR description for each page that visibly changed, and say in one line what to look at. Upload the images by dragging them into the PR on GitHub, or ask the owner to if you cannot; `.qa/` is git-ignored, so never commit them.

## When the change is a flow, not a page

A screenshot cannot show a click, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and run it with a recording:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Attach the video from `test-results/`. Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## Report

Say which pages you shot, what changed in each, and anything you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.
EOF

name: review-to-rule
description: Turn a review correction into a deterministic check (a lint rule, a type or a test) so it never needs saying again. Use when the owner corrects the same kind of mistake twice, says "stop doing X", "always do Y" or "make this a rule", or when a review comment could apply to future code as well as this diff.
---

# Turn a correction into a check

A correction written into AGENTS.md is read sometimes. A check runs every time. Use prose only for what needs human judgment.

## Steps

1. **State the rule in one sentence**, with the reason. If you cannot say why it matters, ask the owner before building anything.
2. **Pick the cheapest check that cannot be ignored**, in this order:
   - **A type.** Make the wrong code fail to compile: a required parameter instead of a default, a branded or narrowed type, a function that only accepts the safe input.
   - **A better API.** One helper in `lib/` that does it right, then a lint rule banning the raw form everywhere else.
   - **A lint rule** in `eslint.config.mjs`. Use `no-restricted-imports` for "this may not import that", `no-restricted-syntax` with an AST selector for "this call or shape is not allowed", `no-restricted-properties` for one member. Write a custom rule in the `moneo` plugin only when a selector cannot express it.
   - **A test**, when the rule is about behaviour and not about how the code is written. Follow AGENTS.md Tests: name the bug it would catch.
3. **Write the error message for an agent.** It must say what is wrong, why, and what to do instead, and point at the AGENTS.md section. "Don't do X" alone leaves the agent to guess; it will add an `eslint-disable`.
4. **Fix every existing violation in the same change.** A rule with a pile of disables teaches agents that disabling is normal. If there are too many to fix now, scope the rule to the folders that are already clean, open an issue for the rest, and widen it later.
5. **Prove it fires.** Lint a one-line bad sample and a good sample:
   `printf '%s\n' 'import { a } from "@/app/page"; export const b = a;' | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename lib/sample.ts`
   Flat config replaces a rule's options when two blocks match the same file, so check a file from every folder the rule should cover.
6. **Trim the prose.** If AGENTS.md already carried this rule as a sentence, shorten it to a pointer at the check, or delete it.
7. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`.

- Write a rule that greps source text or asserts copy.
- Encode a one-off preference about this diff. If it will not recur, just fix the code.

A diagram of states and transitions shows a missing case faster than a diff does. Build it from the code, never from memory of how the flow should work.

---
name: verify-ui
description: Capture before and after screenshots of Moneo pages in light, dark and mobile from the QA app, and attach them to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component or style, when asked to "verify the UI", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
---

# Verify a UI change

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. Give them pictures of every page the change touches.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## Steps

1. **List the pages.** Work out every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names (home widgets, the chat panel, mobile layout).
2. **Get the QA app running** if it is not: `npm run setup -- --qa`, `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base), run:
   `npm run qa:shots -- before /path /other/path`
4. **After.** On the changed code, run the same command with `after`.
   Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`. It prints the HTTP status and any browser console errors per page and exits 1 if there were any.
5. **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark, and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
6. **Show the owner.** Put before and after side by side in the PR description for each page that visibly changed, and say in one line what to look at. Upload the images by dragging them into the PR on GitHub, or ask the owner to if you cannot; `.qa/` is git-ignored, so never commit them.

## When the change is a flow, not a page

A screenshot cannot show a click, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and run it with a recording:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Attach the video from `test-results/`. Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## Report

Say which pages you shot, what changed in each, and anything you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.
EOF
cat > .agents/skills/review-to-rule/SKILL.md <<'EOF'
---
name: review-to-rule
description: Turn a review correction into a deterministic check (a lint rule, a type or a test) so it never needs saying again. Use when the owner corrects the same kind of mistake twice, says "stop doing X", "always do Y" or "make this a rule", or when a review comment could apply to future code as well as this diff.
---

# Turn a correction into a check

A correction written into AGENTS.md is read sometimes. A check runs every time. Use prose only for what needs human judgment.

## Steps

1. **State the rule in one sentence**, with the reason. If you cannot say why it matters, ask the owner before building anything.
2. **Pick the cheapest check that cannot be ignored**, in this order:
   - **A type.** Make the wrong code fail to compile: a required parameter instead of a default, a branded or narrowed type, a function that only accepts the safe input.
   - **A better API.** One helper in `lib/` that does it right, then a lint rule banning the raw form everywhere else.
   - **A lint rule** in `eslint.config.mjs`. Use `no-restricted-imports` for "this may not import that", `no-restricted-syntax` with an AST selector for "this call or shape is not allowed", `no-restricted-properties` for one member. Write a custom rule in the `moneo` plugin only when a selector cannot express it.
   - **A test**, when the rule is about behaviour and not about how the code is written. Follow AGENTS.md Tests: name the bug it would catch.
3. **Write the error message for an agent.** It must say what is wrong, why, and what to do instead, and point at the AGENTS.md section. "Don't do X" alone leaves the agent to guess; it will add an `eslint-disable`.
4. **Fix every existing violation in the same change.** A rule with a pile of disables teaches agents that disabling is normal. If there are too many to fix now, scope the rule to the folders that are already clean, open an issue for the rest, and widen it later.
5. **Prove it fires.** Lint a one-line bad sample and a good sample:
   `printf '%s\n' 'import { a } from "@/app/page"; export const b = a;' | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename lib/sample.ts`
   Flat config replaces a rule's options when two blocks match the same file, so check a file from every folder the rule should cover.
6. **Trim the prose.** If AGENTS.md already carried this rule as a sentence, shorten it to a pointer at the check, or delete it.
7. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`.

## Do not

- Add an `eslint-disable` to make the new rule pass.
- Write a rule that greps source text or asserts copy.
- Encode a one-off preference about this diff. If it will not recur, just fix the code.
EOF
cat > .agents/skills/state-chart/SKILL.md <<'EOF'
---
name: state-chart
description: Draw the state machine of a Moneo flow as a diagram the owner can review, taken from the code. Use when a change adds or alters a multi-step flow (import, bank connect and reconnect, Scalable orders, proposal cards, voice call, agent runs, desktop start-up), when asked to "draw the states", "show the flow" or "state chart", or when a bug looks like an unhandled transition.
---

# Draw a flow's state machine

A diagram of states and transitions shows a missing case faster than a diff does. Build it from the code, never from memory of how the flow should work.

## Steps

1. **Find where the state lives.** Usually a status column in `lib/schema.ts` (and its check constraint in `supabase/migrations/`), a union type, or a workflow in `workflows/`. List every value it can take.
2. **Find every transition.** Grep for each write to that status and each place it is compared. For each one record: from, to, what triggers it (owner tap, AI proposal, background job, bank callback, timeout, failure) and the file and line.
3. **Check it for holes.** Answer each of these from the code:
   - Is every state reachable, and can every state that is not final be left?
   - What happens on failure, on a second tap, and when two devices act at once?
   - What does undo, disconnect and "reset all data" do from each state?
   - What happens if the app quits mid-transition and starts again?
   A question with no answer in the code is a finding. Report it; do not paper over it in the diagram.
4. **Draw it** as Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2`. Name states the way the owner sees them in the app, with the stored value in brackets when it differs. Label each arrow with its trigger. Mark AI-triggered transitions and the ones that need a card the owner accepts.

   ```mermaid
   stateDiagram-v2
     [*] --> Uploaded
     Uploaded --> Reviewing: columns recognised
     Uploaded --> Failed: file unreadable
     Reviewing --> Imported: owner confirms
     Imported --> Uploaded: undo
     Failed --> [*]
   ```

5. **Show it.** For a PR, put the diagram in the description next to the screenshots, with the list of holes from step 3 under it. When the change alters a flow, show the diagram before and after. In chat, render it instead of pasting the source if a preview tool is available.

## Do not

- Commit the diagram to the repo. It goes stale like a comment; regenerate it from the code when needed.
- Invent states or transitions to make the picture tidy.
EOF

cat .claude/skills/verify-ui/SKILL.md | head -8

---
name: state-chart
description: Draw the state machine of a Moneo flow as a diagram the owner can review, taken from the code. Use when a change adds or alters a multi-step flow (import, bank connect and reconnect, Scalable orders, proposal cards, voice call, agent runs, desktop start-up), when asked to "draw the states", "show the flow" or "state chart", or when a bug looks like an unhandled transition.
---

# Draw a flow's state machine

A diagram of states and transitions shows a missing case faster than a diff does. Build it from the code, never from memory of how the flow should work.

## Steps

1. **Find where the state lives.** Usually a status column in `lib/schema.ts` (and its check constraint in `supabase/migrations/`), a union type, or a workflow in `workflows/`. List every value it can take.
2. **Find every transition.** Grep for each write to that status and each place it is compared. For each one record: from, to, what triggers it (owner tap, AI proposal, background job, bank callback, timeout, failure) and the file and line.
3. **Check it for holes.** Answer each of these from the code:
   - Is every state reachable, and can every state that is not final be left?
   - What happens on failure, on a second tap, and when two devices act at once?
   - What does undo, disconnect and "reset all data" do from each state?
   - What happens if the app quits mid-transition and starts again?

   A question with no answer in the code is a finding. Report it; do not paper over it in the diagram.
4. **Draw it** as Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2`. Name states the way the owner sees them in the app, with the stored value in brackets when it differs. Label each arrow with its trigger. Mark AI-triggered transitions and the ones that need a card the owner accepts.

   ```mermaid
   stateDiagram-v2
     [*] --> Uploaded
     Uploaded --> Reviewing: columns recognised
     Uploaded --> Failed: file unreadable
     Reviewing --> Imported: owner confirms
     Imported --> Uploaded: undo
     Failed --> [*]
   ```

5. **Show it.** For a PR, put the diagram in the description next to the screenshots, with the list of holes from step 3 under it. When the change alters a flow, show the diagram before and after. In chat, render it instead of pasting the source if a preview tool is available.

## Do not

- Commit the diagram to the repo. It goes stale like a comment; regenerate it from the code when needed.
- Invent states or transitions to make the picture tidy.

---
name: verify-ui
description: Capture before and after screenshots of Moneo pages in light, dark and mobile from the QA app, and attach them to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component or style, when asked to "verify the UI", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
---

# Verify a UI change

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. Give them pictures of every page the change touches.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## Steps

1. **List the pages.** Work out every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names (home widgets, the chat panel, mobile layout).
2. **Get the QA app running** if it is not: `npm run setup -- --qa`, `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base), run:
   `npm run qa:shots -- before /path /other/path`
4. **After.** On the changed code, run the same command with `after`.
   Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`. It prints the HTTP status and any browser console errors per page and exits 1 if there were any.
5. **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark, and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
6. **Show the owner.** Put before and after side by side in the PR description for each page that visibly changed, and say in one line what to look at. Upload the images by dragging them into the PR on GitHub, or ask the owner to if you cannot; `.qa/` is git-ignored, so never commit them.

## When the change is a flow, not a page

A screenshot cannot show a click, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and run it with a recording:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Attach the video from `test-results/`. Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## Report

Say which pages you shot, what changed in each, and anything you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.

files.content:
# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Moneo ships two ways from this one codebase: the desktop app (`desktop/`, Electron, what most owners install) and the source installation (`npm run setup` + Docker). Every change must work in both.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services: in Docker for the source installation (`docker-compose.yml`), as bundled native processes in the desktop app (`desktop/src/backend/`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`; optional phone access is Tailscale forwarding to it (`lib/phone-access.ts`). Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Private access from the owner's own Tailscale devices needs no login; anything public must add one first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **AI organization labels are the one exception to cards.** The organizer applies high- and medium-confidence category and merchant labels itself, marked as AI (`organized_by = 'ai'`), listed with every other AI decision and undoable; they never become owner rules or owner corrections. Every other AI write is a card.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Moneo ships two ways from this one codebase: the desktop app (`desktop/`, Electron, what most owners install) and the source installation (`npm run setup` + Docker). Every change must work in both.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services: in Docker for the source installation (`docker-compose.yml`), as bundled native processes in the desktop app (`desktop/src/backend/`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`; optional phone access is Tailscale forwarding to it (`lib/phone-access.ts`). Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Private access from the owner's own Tailscale devices needs no login; anything public must add one first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **AI organization labels are the one exception to cards.** The organizer applies high- and medium-confidence category and merchant labels itself, marked as AI (`organized_by = 'ai'`), listed with every other AI decision and undoable; they never become owner rules or owner corrections. Every other AI write is a card.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Never write a comment.** Put the meaning in a name, a type, a test or a lint rule; if a comment would defend a workaround, fix the cause instead. `npm run lint` rejects comments (`moneo/no-comments` in `eslint.config.mjs`) except tool directives such as `eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- reason`.
5. **Corrections become checks.** When a review correction could recur, enforce it with a lint rule, a type or a test whose error message says what to do instead. Add a line here only when it needs human judgment.
6. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts by reproducing the failure; see Tests for when that becomes a kept test. Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot instead.

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's backend (`.env`, Docker project `moneo`, app on port 3000). Tests use the separate test backend below, as its QA user or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the `moneo` Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop its database: that is the owner's financial history. The test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` then `npm run setup -- --qa` starts it fresh.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The desktop app: see Desktop app below.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, the landing page in `docs/` when a headline feature or install step changes, `.env.example` for new variables. Deferred work goes in GitHub issues.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes `.env` secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000)
- Unit: `npm test` · Lint: `npm run lint` · Build: `npm run build` · Bundle budget: `npm run check:bundle` (after a build)
- Database: `npm run test:db` (needs the backend from `npm run setup`)
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)
- Desktop: `node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform <win-x64|mac-arm64|mac-x64|linux-x64>` once, then `npm run desktop:build`, `npm run desktop:dev`, `npm run desktop:dist` and `npm run desktop:smoke` (drives the packaged app)
- Desktop release: push a `v*` tag matching `desktop/package.json`, then publish the drafted release (`desktop/README.md` → Releasing). Never tag or publish unasked.

## Test backend

Everything that needs a database or a running app is tested against `moneo-qa`, never the owner's setup:

- **Backend:** Docker project `moneo-qa` (ports 54521/54522), secrets in the git-ignored `.env.qa` (one shared copy in `~/.moneo/qa.env`, so every worktree uses the same stack). Create, upgrade or copy it into a new worktree with `npm run setup -- --qa`; then `npm run qa:auth` creates the QA user and saves `e2e/.auth.json`.
- **App:** `npm run qa:server` runs this checkout on http://localhost:3100 against `.env.qa`, building into `.next-qa`, with bank access off and a placeholder AI key that every provider rejects, so nothing costs money. `npm run test:e2e` starts it on its own and refuses to run against any server that would sign tests in as the owner.
- **Reset:** `npm run qa:reset` empties the QA workspace. Each spec should still set up the state it needs rather than rely on what earlier runs left behind.
- `npm run test:db` and the `supabase/tests/*.mjs` scripts read `.env.qa` only.
- A nightly run (`npm run qa:nightly`, see `e2e/README.md`) runs every spec twice and keeps the issue "Nightly browser suite is failing" up to date; fix what it lists before adding new specs.

## Desktop app

The Electron app (`desktop/README.md`, `desktop/src/backend/README.md`) runs the same Next.js server as a standalone build next to its own Postgres, GoTrue, PostgREST and Storage processes. There is no Docker, Node.js, terminal or `.env` on the owner's machine, so:

- **Settings the owner needs go in the app**, not in `.env`. `desktop:build` unsets every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` and fails if a local address is baked in; desktop-only behaviour reads `MONEO_DESKTOP_*` at runtime.
- **Migrations run on the owner's existing database** at the next start, after an automatic `pre-upgrade` backup (`desktop/src/backend/migrations.ts`). They must work without the extensions the bundle lacks: supautils, pg_graphql, pg_net, pg_cron, pgsodium/vault, pg_stat_statements, realtime, and uuid-ossp on Windows.
- **The app lives on `http://localhost:47300`** (or the port saved in `shell.json`), not 3000. Derive addresses from the request or `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`; never hard-code a port.
- **Sign-ins open in the system browser** and return through the loopback callbacks; the result reaches the window through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`. The window opens only Moneo's own pages and allows only the microphone and copying.
- **Files the server reads at runtime** by a dynamic path need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`, or the standalone build traces source files and `desktop:build` fails.
- **A new backend service, native module or data folder** must be added to `fetch-backend.mjs`, the start order, backup and restore, and the packaged files in `electron-builder.config.cjs`.
- **Keep the security fuses** (RunAsNode, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `--inspect` off; asar integrity on); `desktop:smoke` reads them back.
- Never test against the owner's installed app or its user-data folder; set `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` to a scratch folder.

The Desktop workflow builds and smoke-tests every platform on pull requests that touch `desktop/`, `scripts/desktop/`, `next.config.ts`, `package*.json` or `supabase/migrations/`.

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `components/` — shared UI
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions
- `desktop/` — the Electron app (`src/` main process, `src/backend/` native backend, `setup/` status window, `bootstrap/` first-run SQL); `scripts/desktop/` builds, packages and smoke-tests it; `.github/workflows/desktop.yml` runs that and drafts releases
- `docs/` — the GitHub Pages landing page (https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/); its download button reads the latest published release

Imports go one way: `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`. `lib/finance/` never imports `lib/ai/`, and Electron stays in `desktop/src`. Lint enforces all of it; code that two layers need lives in the lower one.

## Sign-in callbacks and addresses

Each outside service sends the browser back to a different address. Keep these in mind before changing ports, hosts or remote access:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`): OpenAI only accepts the loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/ai/chatgpt/callback`, so sign-in happens on the computer running Moneo. Tokens are stored there, so chat works from any device afterwards.
- **Enable Banking** (`lib/bank/return-listener.ts`): production apps need an `https://` redirect registered in the Enable Banking app. Moneo uses `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` (a local listener with a cert from `npm run setup`), which forwards to `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **Scalable Capital** (`lib/scalable/server.ts`): dynamic client registration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/api/scalable/callback`. `localhost` registers freely; other hosts need Scalable's allowlist (it rejects `*.ts.net`).
- **Supabase** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `127.0.0.1:54321`): only the server may call it; never send the browser there, or it breaks on other devices.
- **Desktop app**: the same callbacks on the app's own port (47300 by default) instead of 3000.
- **Phone and tablet** (`*.ts.net` through Tailscale Serve): the laptop's addresses above never change. The three logins refuse to start from a remote device (`lib/remote-device.ts`) and say to use the computer; everything else, including sync, works from there.
- **Voice** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for the microphone.

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Tests

A test earns its place by failing when real behaviour breaks. Before writing one, name the bug it would catch.

- **Write tests for** money math, imports and undo, auth, RLS and AI scopes, concurrency, and bugs that actually happened (name the PR or issue).
- **Don't write tests that** assert UI copy or labels, grep source or migration files, mirror the implementation, or need more than about three `vi.mock`s to run. Test the `lib/` function instead.
- One test per behaviour. Don't add a test per requirement or per audit finding; if an existing test covers the failure, extend it.
- `npm test` must pass with no `.env`, no Docker and no network. Anything that needs the database is a `*.live.test.ts`.
- Use fake timers or controlled promises, never real waits. Mock AI, bank and Scalable; real calls are opt-in only.
- Browser specs are for whole user journeys, not single links or labels. Add a spec only when no existing journey can take the check.
- When you remove a feature, remove its tests. Never delete or skip a failing test just to get green: fix the cause, or ask.
- If a pointless test lands, find out why the agent wrote it and fix the guidance here.

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. CI runs the same checks on every pull request.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Deferred work gets their issue created on github.
- Stacked PRs: before merging a PR that another open PR is based on, change the dependent PR's base to `main`; deleting the merged branch otherwise closes it.
- Long agent prompts and plans don't get committed; if guidance must persist, put the rule in AGENTS.md.
- suggest edits in agents.md if there was something that is changed or needs to be there in agents.md but only suggest when it is actually needed dont suggest just for suggesting.(only for prs)

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

gh issue create --title "Guardrails still to build after the audit of PR #223" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
A read-only audit of the guardrails branch (PR #223) listed rules that are still prose or still have more than one way to do them. Each should become a check, not a line in AGENTS.md. Counts are from the audit and worth re-measuring before starting.

## Small

- [ ] **Tests for invariants that only comments stated.** Chart tooltip names are HTML-escaped (`components/chat-chart.tsx`, XSS from a merchant name if dropped); bank connect errors never log the JWT or key (`app/api/bank/connect/route.ts`); the IOU proposal loader never returns `payload` (`lib/ai/iou-actions.ts`).
- [ ] **`server-only`** in `lib/supabase-server.ts`, `lib/service-db.ts`, `lib/service-keys.ts`, `lib/bank/server.ts`, `lib/scalable/server.ts`. Client code is clean today; nothing keeps it so.
- [ ] **One app address helper.** `?? 3000` and `http://localhost:3000` fallbacks in `lib/scheduler.ts`, `lib/phone-access.ts`, `app/settings/ai-access.tsx`, `lib/env.ts`, `lib/remote-device.ts`; then a lint ban on the literal elsewhere.
- [ ] **One cron route wrapper.** The bearer check and service-key lookup are copied in 7 routes under `app/api/cron/`, and the comparison is not timing-safe.
- [ ] **TypeScript flags that cost almost nothing:** `noImplicitReturns` (4 errors), `noImplicitOverride` (1), `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` (0).
- [ ] **`reportUnusedDisableDirectives`** and a fixed budget for `eslint-disable` (6 `exhaustive-deps` disables today).
- [ ] **`lib/safe-action.ts` imports `readableError` from `lib/ai/agent-apply`.** Move it down and forbid `lib/auth`, `lib/settings` and `lib/safe-action` from importing `lib/ai`.
- [ ] **A stored setting the schema does not know breaks every page** with "Moneo could not sign you in" (`settingsSchema.parse` in `lib/auth.ts`; seen with `ai_models.default` in the shared QA workspace). Ignore unknown keys, or fall back per field.

## Medium

- [ ] **One way to make a service-role Supabase client.** `serviceClient` in `lib/service-db.ts` has 5 users; raw `createClient` with the service key appears in about 10 other files.
- [ ] **Environment through `lib/env.ts` only.** 135 `process.env` reads in 42 files, 9 with `!`; the Zod schema covers 4 variables.
- [ ] **Required time zone.** `"Europe/Berlin"` is the default argument of 8 library functions, so a caller that forgets it computes dates in Berlin time. Also inject `now` in `lib/finance` (18 direct clock reads).
- [ ] **One money formatter.** Raw `Intl.NumberFormat` currency formatting in `components/cards/card-view.tsx`, `components/cards/card-chart.tsx`, `components/chat-chart.tsx`, `app/plan/forecast.tsx`; two `formatMoney`. Ban `toFixed` and float maths in `lib/finance` and `lib/import`.
- [ ] **No silent failures.** 52 `.catch(() => {})` and about 20 empty `catch {}`; in `workflows/bank-sync.ts` and `workflows/agent-team.ts` a failed step ends the job with no record.
- [ ] **CI runs the database and browser checks.** `ci.yml` skips `npm run test:db`, `supabase/tests/*.mjs` and Playwright, so RLS, concurrency and precision suites never run on a pull request.
- [ ] **Typed lint** for `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises` and `switch-exhaustiveness-check`, starting with `lib/`, `workflows/` and server actions.
- [ ] **`lib/finance` without request state.** It imports `lib/auth` (7), `lib/settings` (11) and `lib/all-pages` (6); pass the client and settings in.
- [ ] **Hooks for effects and timers** (`usePolling`, `useDismissAfter`), then ban raw `useEffect` and timers in `app/` and `components/` (75 and 25 uses).
- [ ] **Generated database types**, then ban `as unknown as` (27 uses).
- [ ] **Property-based tests** (`fast-check`) for `lib/finance` invariants.

## Large

- [ ] **AI tools get a read-only database type**, so "every AI write is a card" is enforced by the compiler. About 100 write call sites in `lib/ai` today with nothing separating tool handlers from card-apply code.
- [ ] **`noUncheckedIndexedAccess`** by directory (584 errors in non-test code).
- [ ] **A formatter or `max-len`.** 2,361 source lines are over 200 characters.
- [ ] **Generated feature map** of pages, widgets, chat tools and palette entries, checked by a test, to replace most of "Hit every surface".
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

gh pr edit 223 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Moves rules out of prose and review and into lint, so agents get them right by default.

## What changed

- **Comments are banned by lint** (`moneo/no-comments` in `eslint.config.mjs`). Only exact tool directives pass: `eslint-disable* <rule> -- reason`, `@ts-expect-error`, `turbopackIgnore: true`, `@type {…}`, `@vitest-environment`, `/// <reference />`, shebangs. `eslint --fix` removes the rest.
- **3,133 comments removed from 588 files** with that autofix. No code changes in that commit. SQL, CSS, YAML and `.env.example` are outside the rule and untouched.
- **Imports go one way: `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`** (`moneo/import-boundaries`). The rule also rejects `lib/finance` importing `lib/ai`, Electron outside `desktop/`, and app code inside `desktop/src`. It checks static, dynamic, re-exported, `require` and `vi.mock` paths, and each error says where the code belongs.
- **Modules moved to make that true:**
  - `app/money/wealth/net-worth` → `lib/finance/net-worth`
  - `app/money/transactions/input` → `lib/finance/transaction-input`
  - `app/money/recurring/{schedules,suggestions,series}` → `lib/recurring/`
  - `app/ai/agents/actions`, `app/ai/iou-actions` → `lib/ai/agent-actions`, `lib/ai/iou-actions`
  - `app/ai/chat-form`, `app/ai/analysis-panel`, `app/net-worth-chart` → `components/`
- **AGENTS.md:** "never write a comment", "corrections become checks", the import layering, the screenshot command, and a Desktop app section (it only had two passing mentions of Electron).
- **Skills** (`.agents/skills`, with pointers in `.claude/skills`): `verify-ui`, `review-to-rule`, `state-chart`.
- **`npm run qa:shots -- <label> home money/transactions`** saves each page from the QA app in light, dark and mobile to `.qa/shots/<label>/` and exits 1 on a console error or failed request. It refuses port 3000.

A second agent audited the branch; its findings about these rules are fixed here, and the rest are in #224.

## Checks

`npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm run check:bundle` pass. `npx vitest run --testTimeout=60000` passes (1701 tests). With the default 5 s timeout a few first-test-in-file timeouts appear on my Windows machine; an agent saw the same ones on a copy without these changes.

`qa:shots` was run against this checkout's QA app for Home and Transactions in all three views.

Not run: Playwright and the desktop build. The moves change import paths only. The last build ran before the analysis panel moved; typecheck and tests ran after.

EOF
